unit: Geometry · Chapter I. Volumes of solids
source: Based on the topics of the Armenian grade 12 mathematics textbooks (general stream)

stages.headline: Cavalieri's principle: if every plane parallel to a given one cuts two solids in sections of equal area, the solids have equal volumes.
stages.headlineEnglish: Cavalieri's principle: if every plane parallel to a given one cuts two solids in sections of equal area, the solids have equal volumes.

stages.headline: Example: an oblique and a right parallelepiped with the same base and height have equal volumes.
stages.headlineEnglish: Example: an oblique and a right parallelepiped with the same base and height have equal volumes.

stages.headline: A volume can also be found by cutting the solid into parts or completing it to a known solid.
stages.headlineEnglish: A volume can also be found by cutting the solid into parts or completing it to a known solid.

stages.headline: By Cavalieri's principle, which solids have equal volumes?
stages.headlineEnglish: By Cavalieri's principle, which solids have equal volumes?

choices: those with sections of equal area
